test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 16 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The Integrated Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2023 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 11 August 2023, which amends the __________________.

options.text: Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2017
Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2016
Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2014
Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2015

solution:
The correct answer is __**Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2017**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Integrated Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2023 was introduced to amend the **IGST Act, 2017**.
 
• The IGST Act, 2017 governs the inter-state supply of goods and services in India.
 
• The amendment aims to address issues and enhance the implementation of the IGST Act.
 
• The bill was introduced in the **Lok Sabha on 11 August 2023**.
 
• This amendment is part of the continuous efforts to refine and improve the Goods and Services Tax (GST) framework in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**

 
 
• GST is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based tax that is levied on every value addition.
 
• It was implemented in India on 1 July 2017, replacing multiple indirect taxes previously levied by the central and state governments.
 
• GST is divided into three parts: CGST (Central GST), SGST (State GST), and IGST (Integrated GST).
 
 
 
• **Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST)**
 
 
• IGST is applicable on inter-state transactions and imports.
 
• It is collected by the central government and then distributed between the central and state governments.
 
• IGST ensures that the tax is levied only once for inter-state transactions, thereby avoiding double taxation.
 
 
 
• **Inter-state vs Intra-state Transactions**
 
 
• Inter-state transactions involve the supply of goods or services from one state to another.
 
• Intra-state transactions are those where the supply occurs within the same state.
 
• CGST and SGST are applicable on intra-state transactions, while IGST is applicable on inter-state transactions.
 
 
 
• **GST Council**
 
 
• The GST Council is the governing body responsible for regulating GST in India.
 
• It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes state finance ministers.
 
• The council makes recommendations on various aspects of GST, including tax rates, exemptions, and amendments.
